CHIEF COMPLAINT: Follow-up for proliferative diabetic retinopathy, right eye, s/p panretinal photocoagulation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 58-year-old male with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus, HbA1c 9.1%, presents for scheduled follow-up laser session. He underwent initial panretinal photocoagulation to the right eye 8 days ago for high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy with neovascularization of the disc. He reports mild floaters but denies new flashes, curtain-like vision loss, or worsening blurriness. He is currently within the global surgical period of the initial laser procedure.

OCULAR HISTORY: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy OD, moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy OS. No prior vitrectomy.

EXAMINATION:
VA OD 20/50, OS 20/30 (unchanged from prior visit).
IOP 16 OD, 15 OS.
Anterior segment: quiet, no rubeosis.
Dilated fundus exam OD: scattered laser scars in mid and far periphery consistent with recent PRP, residual neovascularization of the disc still visible with reduced but persistent activity, no vitreous hemorrhage.
OS: dot-blot hemorrhages, no neovascularization at this time, PRP not yet indicated.

ASSESSMENT: Persistent neovascularization of the disc, right eye, despite initial panretinal photocoagulation performed 8 days ago. The residual risk of visual loss from ongoing neovascular activity continues to outweigh the risks of additional laser treatment, and further scatter laser is clinically warranted to consolidate treatment.

PLAN: Proceed today with a supplemental panretinal photocoagulation session to the right eye to treat previously untreated peripheral retina and reinforce areas of persistent neovascularization, as this remains within the 90-day global period of the index procedure performed on this eye. Discussed with patient that this session is being billed as part of the global package of the initial procedure rather than as a separate reimbursable service, consistent with payer policy, since it falls within the postoperative period of the initial treatment. Continue close diabetic retinal surveillance; consider anti-VEGF adjunct if neovascularization does not regress by next visit in 2 weeks. Reinforce glycemic control with endocrinology.
